fichas.lema: what it is and how it shows up
fichas.oQueE: A mass politics that promises national rebirth against an imagined decline, exalts a leader and a "pure" people, and treats part of society as an internal enemy. It uses lies and violence as method, allied with elites who profit from the order it imposes.
comoAparece: Cult of a mythic past: "things were better back then"
Contempt for truth and for science
An internal enemy always at hand
The dominant group claims to be persecuted
The law binds the enemy, not the ally
Attacks on the press, universities and schools
fichas.comoSeDefender: Name the mechanism, not the label ("that is an invented enemy"). Check the source and who pays. Distrust urgency and tailor-made anger. Protect those who investigate and teach.
fichas.fonte: Eco, "Ur-Fascism" (1995) · Paxton, The Anatomy of Fascism (2004) · Stanley, How Fascism Works (2018) · Arendt, The Origins of Totalitarianism (1951)

fichas.lema: from the money to the headline
fichas.oQueE: The machine that manufactures and spreads lies at scale. It is not one liar: it is a chain.
comoAparece: The chain: who pays, the agency, the influencer, the account network, the headline
The same sentence in many accounts at the same time
Emotional urgency: "share before they delete it"
No source, or a source that cites itself
The same target of hatred in every version
fichas.comoSeDefender: Stop before you share. Look for the origin. Be wary of synchrony. Prefer those who correct their mistakes over those who never do.
fichas.fonte: Paul and Matthews, "The Russian Firehose of Falsehood Propaganda Model", RAND (2016): the volume-and-repetition model, useful as a general mechanism

fichas.oQueE: The question that clears the smoke: who does this serve? Behind much political conflict lies an economic interest the speeches never mention: extraction, rent-seeking, the sale of security and arms, the attention economy.
comoAparece: The speech talks about values: family, homeland, order, "development"
The decision delivers a profit to someone
The bill is almost never read aloud
fichas.comoSeDefender: Follow the money: who pays for the campaign, who gains from the law, who owns the channel. Compare the speech with what the decision delivers.
fichas.fonte: General mechanism. The game cites no number without a public source (INPE/PRODES and MapBiomas, for deforestation).

fichas.oQueE: Fear as a method of government: keep people frightened so that they accept what they would not accept calmly.
comoAparece: An invented internal enemy
Moral panic: a hand-picked topic takes over the whole conversation
Security as spectacle: force is shown, results are not
While everyone watches the fear, the wallet and the land change owners
fichas.comoSeDefender: Ask what really changed (prices, rights, land) while everyone was looking the other way. Tailor-made fear is a sign.
fichas.fonte: Stanley (2018) · Eco (1995) · Cohen, Folk Devils and Moral Panics (1972)

fichas.lema: the agenda and the silence have an owner
fichas.oQueE: What information becomes when ownership is concentrated and advertising pays the bills: the agenda and the silence have an owner.
comoAparece: Opinion dressed up as news
What goes unsaid: the story that disappears
Repetition that looks like consensus
Selective criticism: one side is investigated, the other only commented on
fichas.comoSeDefender: Tell news, opinion and propaganda apart. Read sources with more than one owner. Look for the reporting, not just the headline.
fichas.fonte: General mechanism of the political economy of communication (Herman and Chomsky, Manufacturing Consent, 1988). In the game the media is an archetype, the "Full Truth Network": satire, not a portrait.

fichas.oQueE: This is satire, and the game says so. It claims nothing about any real person: it is the mirror of the archetypes.
comoAparece: The "patriot" who sells the country for a good contract
The "anti-state" figure who lives on tax breaks and subsidies
The "defender of life" who cuts hospital beds
The "liberal" who asks for censorship when the subject is themselves
fichas.comoSeDefender: Compare what is said with what is done: inconsistency is the first sign that the speech serves something else.
fichas.fonte: Declared satire: no claim of fact.
